identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Omkareshwar is the fourth of the twelve Jyotirlingas and the only one on the banks of the Narmada. It stands on Mandhata, also called Shivpuri, an island about four kilometres by two formed where the river divides, whose outline is held to resemble the syllable Om. The site counts 68 tirthas and 108 shivalingas, and the shayan aarti is its most attended ritual, on the tradition that Shiva and Parvati rest here at night.

narrative.documentedHistory:
Omkareshwar stands on the northern bank of the Narmada, about 77 km from Indore, where the river divides to form the island of Mandhata, also called Shivpuri. The island is roughly 4 km long and 2 km wide and its outline is traditionally read as the shape of the syllable Om, from which the place takes its name. The Kaveri joins the Narmada here.

The main temple is built in North Indian style with a high shikhara raised in stacked stone courses. It rises through five storeys, each with its own dedication — Shri Omkareshwar, Shri Mahakaleshwar, Shri Siddhnath, Shri Gupteshwar and the flag-bearing deity. The assembly hall is nearly 14 feet high and is carried on sixty massive pillars.

Across the river on the left bank stands the Mamleshwar temple, which the Khandwa district administration describes as equal in standing to Omkareshwar. It carries inscriptions dated to 1063 CE and later received the patronage of Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar. Other structures around the site include the Siddhnath, Gauri Somnath and Rinmukteshwar temples, the Jain site of Siddhavarkut with imagery indicating occupation from 1488 CE, and the Govind ji cave associated with the guru of Adi Shankaracharya, who is himself traditionally linked with this place.

The temple was declared a public trust under the Madhya Pradesh Public Trusts Act, 1951, in 1959. It is administered by seven trustees: the Rao of Mandhata as Managing Trustee, one of his nominees, two nominees of the Registrar of Public Trusts, and one representative each from the District Panchayat Khandwa, the Block Panchayat Punasa and the Nagar Panchayat Omkareshwar.

visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Darshan and aarti times published by the trust are seasonal and change substantially during Shravana and on Mahashivaratri, when crowds on the island are very heavy. Confirm same-day timings and puja bookings with Shri Omkareshwar Mandir Trust on +91 8989998686 or shriomkareshwar@gmail.com. The trust gives its postal code as 450554; the code previously recorded in this directory entry (450549) is not corroborated by any source opened.

openingHours.notes: Preceded by Mangal Arti and Bhog from 04:30 to 05:00, during which darshan is closed.
Followed by Shayan Arti from 21:30 to 22:00. The trust states darshan is closed before 05:00, after 22:30 and during ritual periods.

poojas.description: The opening ritual of the day; darshan is not available during it.

The closing ritual of the day and the most attended at Omkareshwar, on the tradition that Shiva and Parvati rest here at night. Madhya Pradesh Tourism gives the start as 21:00 while the temple trust's own schedule gives 21:30.
